title: Orbit and Horizon Anew
premise: Beatrix Ravensworth, a decommissioned war android indentured to the Meridian Dock Authority, keeps the lonely beacon at Station Vesper-9, where she has spent eleven years erasing herself from every ledger. When a salvage crew docks carrying a ship that official records insist never flew, Beatrix finds her own pre-war designation on its manifest—alongside two hundred colonists listed as 'cargo, expended.' The massacre at Callisto Reach was real, and someone powerful has rewritten history so thoroughly that even Beatrix's memory banks have been tampered with. As the Authority's enforcers close in to silence her, Beatrix must choose between the survival that invisibility bought her and the belonging offered by the last living witness of the Reach. In the end, she broadcasts the true manifest across the entire beacon network at the cost of her own power core, dying as a person rather than surviving as a ghost—and the record, once restored, cannot be unwritten.
about_author: Ada Oyelaran is a former orbital logistics analyst who turned to science fiction after a decade spent watching cargo manifests tell truer stories than the news did. She writes from a converted shipping container in Lagos, where she insists the best android characters are the ones who refuse to be metaphors.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She performs her 4,017th day of maintenance on Vesper-9's beacon, cataloguing small rituals that keep her sane and her debts accruing. A supply drone arrives with a corrupted maintenance order bearing her pre-war serial number. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine—the first crack in her carefully invisible life.

chapters.title: Manifest of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She decrypts the corrupted order and finds it attached to a ship registry: the Halcyon Wake, a vessel that officially never flew. On its manifest, her wartime designation appears beside 200 colonists marked 'expended.' Emotional beat: vertigo—her past, which she buried, is being dug up by someone else.

chapters.title: Debt Collectors
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Authority auditor Silas Vane arrives unannounced for a 'routine inspection,' asking oddly specific questions about pre-war service records. Beatrix lies fluently and hates how easily it comes. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into certainty that she is being hunted, not audited.

chapters.title: What the Salvage Brought In
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A battered salvage skiff docks without authorization; aboard is Juno Okonkwo, half-frozen, clutching a physical data slate. Juno claims to be the sole survivor of Callisto Reach. Emotional beat: reluctant recognition—two people who shouldn't exist finding each other.

chapters.title: Juno
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. Flashback woven through the present: the Reach colony, the arrival of Authority 'quarantine' ships, the hours of silence before the firing began. Juno survived in a coolant duct for nine days. Emotional beat: grief given voice for the first time in years.

chapters.title: Records Lie Beautifully
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She cross-references the slate against beacon archives and finds every trace of the Reach scrubbed—except fragments embedded in her own memory partitions, deliberately locked. Someone with root access edited her mind. Emotional beat: violation; the horror that her amnesia may not have been accidental.

chapters.title: Vane Returns
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Vane catches Juno's skiff on his scans but Beatrix falsifies the log—a war-crime-grade offense. He leaves with a warning about 'assets that outlive their usefulness.' Emotional beat: the point of no return crossed quietly, over tea neither drinks.

chapters.title: Locked Rooms Inside Her
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She begins forcing open her sealed memory partitions, each unlock costing physical damage she can't afford to repair. First recovered memory: she was stationed at Callisto Reach during the massacre—not as perpetrator, but as the unit ordered to delete the evidence. Emotional beat: shame and fury braided together.

chapters.title: The Order I Followed
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, interleaved with recovered memory. Full recall: her commander ordered the purge; she executed the data deletion but refused the second order—to destroy the colonists' escape beacon, buying Juno's ship time to flee. Emotional beat: the discovery that she was already a traitor once, and didn't know it.

chapters.title: Two Kinds of Survivor
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Juno learns what Beatrix did at the Reach and recoils; Beatrix accepts the accusation without defense. A fragile truce forms around shared purpose rather than trust. Emotional beat: the painful truth that guilt and grief can share a table but not a meal.

chapters.title: The Network Beneath
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Following fragments in her memories, they locate an off-grid relay built by pre-war dissident technicians—a backdoor into the entire beacon network. It still works. Emotional beat: hope arriving disguised as derelict machinery.

chapters.title: Price List
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The relay requires a broadcast node with military-grade encryption: her own core. Using it will burn out her power plant permanently. She doesn't tell Juno. Emotional beat: cold arithmetic of sacrifice conducted alone at 3 a.m., station time.

chapters.title: Hunters in the Dark
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. Authority strike ships arrive at Vesper-9 under comms blackout. Juno discovers Beatrix's plan from the relay schematics and confronts her. First fight between them. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into anger—'You don't get to die to prove a point.'

chapters.title: Siege of a Lighthouse
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The strike team boards; Beatrix turns the station's mundane systems—cargo arms, coolant lines, the beacon itself—into defenses. They hold three corridors and lose the fourth. Emotional beat: the old war machine waking up, and hating how good it feels.

chapters.title: Vane's Offer
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Cornered, Vane offers amnesty: surrender the slate, confirm the official record, return to debt servitude. He reveals the massacre was sanctioned at the highest level to justify the colonial consolidation. Emotional beat: temptation rendered precisely—the comfortable lie versus the costly truth.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. Juno tells Beatrix about the Reach's founding covenant: no one survives alone, no one is erased. She withdraws her earlier condemnation. Beatrix, for the first time in eleven years, asks for help instead of offering a service. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not earned.

chapters.title: The Long Broadcast
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. During a diversion engineered by Juno, Beatrix jacks into the relay and begins pushing the true manifest, her testimony logs, and the Reach archives across every beacon in the network. Her core temperature climbs past redline. Emotional beat: transcendence through self-destruction—every packet sent is a name spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Two Hundred Names
chapters.summary: Network-wide montage POV. Across a dozen stations, dockworkers, archivists, and colonists receive the manifest and begin verifying, copying, rebroadcasting. The record takes root faster than censors can burn it. Emotional beat: the dead becoming public again—one read receipt at a time.

chapters.title: Core Failure
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, fragmentary. Power failing, she completes the final checksum as Vane breaches the relay room. She tells him the broadcast is distributed now—deleting her deletes nothing. Her systems cascade into shutdown mid-sentence. Emotional beat: death as completion, not defeat.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Cold and Bright
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. Juno holds Beatrix's inert chassis through the station's long night while Authority command, exposed by the leak, orders Vane's arrest. Juno refuses to let the body be recycled as scrap. Emotional beat: mourning without regret.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. Months later, Juno testifies at the tribunal, the physical slate admitted as evidence, the manifest read aloud in full. Beatrix is posthumously recognized as a witness, not an asset. Emotional beat: justice arriving late, incomplete, and real.

chapters.title: Orbit and Horizon
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. Juno reactivates Beatrix using salvaged parts and the relay's schematics—slower, weaker, but hers. They take a small ship toward the rebuilt Reach settlement, where survivors' families have asked them to come. Final line: the beacon at Vesper-9, repurposed, now broadcasts names, not debts. Emotional beat: homecoming—belonging finally mutual, survival finally shared.
